questions.q: Why does the summary say pictures of babies make advertisements more effective?
a: Infant faces trigger emotion almost instantly
Babies are cheaper to photograph than adults
Viewers feel guilty and keep looking away
Baby images contain less text to read
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the brain's emotional area responds within a few hundred milliseconds, an attention to infants that is hard-wired for survival.

questions.q: Where should a baby in an ad be looking, according to the summary?
a: At the product or headline you want noticed
Directly at the viewer at all times
Away from the camera into empty space
At another baby in the same picture
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites James Breeze's finding that viewers follow the gaze of the person in an image, so the baby should look at the product.

questions.q: What does the summary say about speaking into someone's right ear?
a: People tend to trust what they hear on that side
It makes your voice sound louder to them
It prevents them from remembering the request
It works only in noisy nightclub settings
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites Italian research showing that requests are more likely to succeed when delivered on the listener's right side.

questions.q: What did Al Roth's ultimatum game research show about casual conversation?
a: Small talk sharply increased fair offers and reduced rejections
Talking before the game made offers more selfish
Conversation had no effect on the final outcome
Participants who talked refused to split the money
questions.why: Lesson 2 reports that letting participants talk produced 83 percent more fair offers and only 5 percent rejections.

questions.q: Why does surprise capture attention so effectively, according to the summary?
a: It interrupts the brain's prediction of what comes next
It overloads the senses so people stop thinking
It makes familiar phrases easier to remember
It triggers the same response as a baby's face
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the hippocampus predicts events from cues, so something unexpected like a random word forces a reaction.
